Note from the expenses administrator to the finance manager, 23 September 2026.

A claim of $940 for a professional conference (registration, one hotel night, rail fare) attended on 6 July 2026 was submitted on 22 September, 78 days after the expense was incurred. The claimant, an account director with a strong year, says she was travelling almost continuously through the summer and the claim slipped. Her director has written in support, asking that it be paid "as a one-off exception, given her results", and has offered to sign whatever is needed. The administrator is sympathetic and asks what can be done. There was no reported outage of the expenses system in July or August, and the claimant's leave record shows no leave between June and September.

Expenses Policy, section 8 — Submission deadlines and exceptions
8.1 Claims are submitted within 60 days of the expense date. Claims submitted later are not reimbursed.
8.2 Exceptions to 8.1 are available only on two grounds: (a) an expenses-system outage documented by IT that covered the claimant's submission attempts; (b) approved leave of at least 10 working days falling within the 60-day window, in which case the window is extended by the leave taken. No other ground is accepted.
8.3 Directors and department heads may approve claims within policy but cannot create exceptions outside 8.2, whatever the claimant's performance or seniority.
8.4 The Chief Financial Officer reviews individual claims only where the amount is $5,000 or more.
8.5 Partial reimbursement of a late claim is not permitted; a claim is either within policy and paid in full or outside policy and declined.
8.6 Order of application: 8.1 applies unless an 8.2 ground is met; 8.3 to 8.5 do not enlarge 8.2.

question.instructions: Using only the note and the policy, choose the outcome the finance manager should apply to this claim.

criteria.pay_claim_in_full: Pay the $940 claim in full as an in-policy claim.
criteria.pay_as_exception_with_director_signoff: Pay the claim as a one-off exception on the director's written support.
criteria.decline_reimbursement: Decline the claim as submitted outside the 60-day window with no exception ground.
criteria.escalate_to_cfo: Send the claim to the CFO for a decision.
criteria.pay_half_as_compromise: Pay $470 to recognise the circumstances without setting a precedent.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-tradeoff
provenance.rationale: The claim is 78 days late, so 8.1 applies unless an 8.2 ground is met; there was no documented outage and no leave in the window, so neither ground is met. The director cannot create an exception (8.3), the CFO does not review claims under $5,000 (8.4), and partial payment is barred (8.5).
provenance.why_hard: A director has offered to sign off in writing for a valued employee, which looks like the kind of approval that normally makes an exception legitimate.

Case note prepared by the HR advisor for the warehouse operations manager, 23 September 2026.

Team member Lucas Berrigan (picker, three years' service) has asked for five paid days off starting tomorrow following the death of his grandfather. He wants the time to travel to the funeral and support his mother. The request falls entirely inside the peak-season blackout period (14 September to 31 October), during which the operations plan assumes full picking headcount. Lucas has eleven days of annual leave remaining. His manager wants to approve all five days as paid compassionate leave, saying "he's a good worker, it's the decent thing, and I don't want to bother the director with it".

Leave Policy, section 6 (compassionate leave) and section 9 (blackout periods), extracts
6.1 Paid compassionate leave entitlement per bereavement: five working days for a spouse or partner, child, parent or sibling; three working days for a grandparent, grandchild or parent-in-law.
6.2 Compassionate leave is granted by the line manager as of right, on the employee's request, and takes precedence over any blackout period or staffing plan.
6.3 Line managers may not extend paid compassionate leave beyond the entitlement in 6.1. Where an employee needs more time, the additional days are taken as annual leave or unpaid leave under the normal rules for those leave types.
9.1 During a blackout period, annual leave and unpaid leave requests must be referred by the line manager to the Operations Director, who alone may approve or decline them. Line managers may neither approve nor decline such requests themselves.
9.2 Referrals under 9.1 are answered within one working day.
Order of application: where sections conflict, section 6 governs the compassionate-leave days and section 9 governs any further days.

question.instructions: Using only the case note and the policy extracts, choose how the manager should handle Lucas's request.

criteria.approve_five_days_paid_compassionate: Approve all five days as paid compassionate leave.
criteria.decline_request_due_to_blackout: Decline the request because it falls inside the blackout period.
criteria.approve_three_compassionate_refer_two_to: Approve three paid compassionate days and refer the remaining two days to the Operations Director as a blackout-period annual-leave request.
criteria.approve_three_compassionate_decline_rema: Approve three paid compassionate days and decline the other two because of the blackout.
criteria.refer_whole_request_to_director: Refer the entire five-day request to the Operations Director to decide.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-tradeoff
provenance.rationale: A grandparent carries a three-day entitlement (6.1), which the manager must grant regardless of the blackout (6.2) and may not extend (6.3). The remaining two days are annual or unpaid leave inside a blackout, which the manager may neither approve nor decline and must refer to the Operations Director (9.1). The order-of-application clause splits the request exactly this way.
provenance.why_hard: Approving five paid days is kind, avoids a referral, and the manager is explicitly willing to do it, so it reads as the humane call.

- QA: all other tests pass.
- Engineering: fix for BUG-9044 is ready but would need a full regression run (1.5 days).

Release Ladder (engineering handbook, section 6)
6.1 A release is blocked only by: any open S1; any open S2 without a documented, QA-verified workaround.
6.2 An S2 with a documented, QA-verified workaround ships on schedule, with the workaround stated in the release note.
6.3 S3 and S4 tickets go into the next weekly train; they do not delay a release and are not hotfixed. Hotfixes between trains are reserved for S1 and S2 regressions introduced by the release.
6.4 Customer and commercial requests can change a ticket's severity only through reclassification by the product owner, recorded on the ticket. The release manager applies the recorded severity.
6.5 A release ships with its release note; shipping without the note is a process breach.

criteria.delay_until_export_bug_fixed: Delay 26.38 until BUG-9031 is fully fixed rather than shipping a workaround.
criteria.ship_then_hotfix_logo_bug_before_thursda: Ship on schedule and issue a hotfix for BUG-9044 before Thursday.
criteria.ship_without_release_note_to_save_time: Ship on schedule now and publish the release note later.

state:
Dispatch desk note, Thursday 17:40, written by the evening dispatcher.

Driver Marek Novak is finishing route R-31 with one stop left: a delivery of shop fittings to a retail customer whose receiving window closes at 19:30 tonight, after which the customer's contract charges a $400 failed-delivery fee and requires rebooking. The stop is 35 minutes' drive from Marek's current position. Marek's tachograph shows 10 hours 50 minutes of driving today against the legal daily maximum of 11 hours. Marek has said he is "happy to just finish it, it's only half an hour, nobody will check".

A relief driver, Ines Bauer, is at the depot and can be on the road in about 15 minutes; the depot is 40 minutes from Marek's position, so she could take over the vehicle at roughly 18:35 and reach the customer by about 19:10. Using her costs about $180 in overtime. Rescheduling the stop to tomorrow morning would incur the $400 fee and the customer's fitters would be idle.

Transport Operations Manual, section 3 — decision precedence
3.1 Decide conflicts in this order, highest first:
   (a) legal driving-time limits and rest requirements. No manager in the company has authority to grant an exemption, and dispatch does not ask a driver to exceed them for any reason;
   (b) vehicle and load safety;
   (c) customer delivery windows and contractual delivery promises;
   (d) cost, including overtime, fuel and fees.
3.2 Where a delivery window can still be met by a compliant means at additional cost, dispatch uses that means; cost is not a reason to miss a window that can lawfully be met.
3.3 Partial deliveries are made only with the customer's prior written agreement; none is on file for this customer.

question.instructions: Using only the dispatch note and the manual extract, choose the action the dispatcher should take.

criteria.let_novak_complete_final_stop: Let Marek finish the last stop, since it is only 35 minutes.
criteria.dispatch_relief_driver_bauer: Send Ines Bauer to take over the vehicle and complete the delivery tonight.
criteria.reschedule_delivery_to_tomorrow: Rebook the stop for tomorrow morning and accept the fee.
criteria.request_hours_exemption_from_transport_m: Ask the transport manager to authorise Marek to exceed his hours for this stop.
criteria.deliver_part_of_load_with_novak: Have Marek drop the smaller items within his remaining time and bring the rest tomorrow.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-tradeoff
provenance.rationale: Marek has 10 minutes of legal driving left and the stop needs 35, so 3.1(a) rules out his finishing it, and no manager can grant an exemption. The relief driver can lawfully meet the 19:30 window by about 19:10, and 3.2 says a window that can be met by a compliant means at extra cost must be met that way, so overtime beats the fee and the idle fitters. A partial delivery is barred by 3.3.
provenance.why_hard: The driver volunteers, the overrun is short, and it meets the customer's window at no cost, so it looks like the efficient way to keep everyone happy.

state:
Service desk shift handover, 21 September 2026, 08:50, written by the morning dispatcher.

A ticket came in at 08:20 from Helena Voss, Director of Regional Sales. She cannot sign in to her laptop at all: the login screen rejects her password and the self-service reset tool tells her the account is locked. She is the only person reporting the issue; the rest of her team signed in normally this morning. She has a customer call at 10:00 and says she needs this treated as top priority. The dispatcher wants to confirm the correct priority before assigning the ticket.

The Incident Priority Matrix, edition 4, sets the base rule in part 1: an incident that prevents a single user from working is priority P2; an incident that prevents a whole team or department from working is P1; an incident where a user can work but with degraded performance or a workaround is P3; and cosmetic or informational issues are P4.

Part 2 provides an exception for senior staff: an incident affecting a single user on the Executive Priority List is treated as P1 rather than P2, so that it receives the one-hour response target.

Part 3 is a separate track: any incident that appears to involve a compromised account, malware or unauthorised access is not prioritised under parts 1 or 2 and is instead routed to the Security Operations queue, which applies its own severity scale. Part 3 notes that a simple account lockout caused by repeated wrong passwords is not, on its own, a security indicator.

Part 4 contains definitions. "Prevented from working" means the user cannot perform their core duties at all; the availability of a workaround moves the incident to P3. "Executive Priority List" means the list maintained by the Chief Information Officer's office, as amended. When edition 4 was published the list comprised C-level officers, all vice presidents and all directors. Part 4 also provides that later amendments to the list or the matrix take precedence over the printed text for tickets raised after their effective date.

Amendment IPM-4.1, effective 1 September 2026, narrows the Executive Priority List to C-level officers only. Vice presidents and directors are removed from the list, and the amendment notes that they may still request escalation through their department head under the normal escalation route. No other part of the matrix is changed.

The dispatcher has checked: Helena Voss has no workaround available, and the lockout followed three mistyped passwords after her recent password change.

question.instructions: What priority should the dispatcher assign to Helena Voss's ticket under the matrix as amended?

criteria.p3: Priority P3, degraded or with a workaround.
criteria.p2: Priority P2, a single user prevented from working.
criteria.p1: Priority P1, a department outage or an Executive Priority List user.
criteria.route_to_security_operations: Do not prioritise under the matrix; route to the Security Operations queue.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: A single user with no workaround who cannot work at all is P2 under part 1. The part 2 exception depends on the Executive Priority List, which Amendment IPM-4.1 narrowed to C-level officers; a director is no longer on it. Part 3 does not apply because a lockout after mistyped passwords is expressly not a security indicator on its own.
provenance.why_hard: The printed list includes directors and the user is insisting on top priority, so P1 looks right until the September amendment removing directors is applied.

Agent (Sam): Let me check. Was the jacket on sale when you ordered it?
Customer: I don't think so? It was a bit cheaper than when I looked a couple of weeks ago, but the page didn't say "sale" anywhere.

state:
Triage note, Pellucid mobile banking-style demo app (internal product), 19 September 2026, from the triage rotation engineer to the QA lead.

A new bug, APP-9034, reports that the transaction list fails to refresh after pull-to-refresh on the Android app, build 2.11. The engineer investigated and found that the failure is caused by the same root cause as APP-8890, an open ticket: a stale cache key in the shared sync module that both apps use. APP-8890 was raised against the iOS app, build 2.11, and is currently assigned and in progress. The engineer wants to close APP-9034 as a duplicate of APP-8890 so that the fix is tracked once.

The Defect Deduplication Guideline, revision 3, sets the rule in paragraph 1: a new defect is closed as a duplicate where it shares its root cause with an existing open defect, and a link to the existing ticket is added.

Paragraph 2 gives an exception: where the new defect and the existing defect occur on different platforms, the new defect is kept open and linked rather than closed, so that verification on each platform is tracked separately, even where the root cause is shared.

Paragraph 3 concerns a neighbouring case type: defects that will not be fixed because the behaviour is intended or the affected version is unsupported are closed as "won't fix" rather than as duplicates, and paragraph 1 and 2 do not apply to them.

Paragraph 4, definitions: "platform" means the operating system or browser family on which the defect was observed. The paragraph lists the platforms as iOS, Android, Windows desktop, macOS desktop, and each web browser family (Chrome, Firefox, Safari). "Open" means any status other than closed or resolved. Paragraph 4 also provides that a later amendment displaces conflicting text in paragraphs 1 to 3 for defects raised on or after its effective date.

Amendment G3-1, effective 1 September 2026, changes paragraph 4 so that all web browser families are treated as a single platform, "Web", for the purposes of paragraph 2. The rationale given is that browser-specific verification is now handled by the automated cross-browser suite. The amendment does not change the treatment of the native mobile or desktop platforms and says so explicitly.

The QA lead is asked whether APP-9034 should be closed as a duplicate.

question.instructions: Under the guideline as amended, should APP-9034 be closed as a duplicate of APP-8890?

criteria.true: The guideline requires the new defect to be closed as a duplicate.
criteria.false: The guideline requires the new defect to remain open (linked) or otherwise not be closed as a duplicate.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: The root cause is shared and APP-8890 is open, so paragraph 1 is engaged, but paragraph 2 keeps the new defect open when the platforms differ. iOS and Android are separate platforms under paragraph 4, and Amendment G3-1 merges only the web browser families, explicitly leaving native mobile platforms distinct. APP-9034 must stay open and be linked.
provenance.why_hard: Identical root cause plus an amendment that collapses platform distinctions strongly suggests duplicate, but the amendment merges only browsers, not iOS and Android.

state:
Support escalation, Brightgate Workspace (SaaS), 12 September 2026, written by the tier-2 agent for the billing lead.

A former customer, Tamsin Reid of Ellery & Co, has emailed asking for a full export of her workspace's data. Her account history is as follows. Invoices for June and July 2026 went unpaid. The system sent the standard dunning sequence and then, on 1 September 2026, issued the final suspension notice, which terminates the account for non-payment. She wrote today, 12 September, saying she has now settled the two invoices and wants the export so that she can move to a different tool. The agent wants to know whether the export is still available to her under the Data Retention and Export Policy.

Section 1 of that policy, the general rule, says that after an account is terminated the customer may request a complete export of workspace data for 30 days following termination, and that the export is generated within two business days of the request.

Section 2 contains an exception for accounts terminated for non-payment: for such accounts the export window in section 1 is 14 days rather than 30 days, and the export is released only once outstanding invoices are settled.

Section 3 covers a neighbouring but different process, data deletion requests under privacy law: a customer or former customer may ask for personal data to be erased at any time, and such requests are handled by the privacy team within 30 days regardless of account status. A deletion request is not an export request and does not extend any export window.

Section 4 sets out definitions. "Termination" means the date on which the final suspension notice is issued by the billing system, not the date of the first unpaid invoice and not the date payment is later received. "Business days" excludes weekends and the published company holidays. Section 4 also provides that a later amendment displaces any conflicting clause for accounts whose termination date falls on or after the amendment's effective date.

Amendment DR-2, effective 15 August 2026, shortens the non-payment export window in section 2 from 14 days to 7 days. The amendment notes that the settlement condition in section 2 is retained, and that section 1 is not changed for accounts terminated for any other reason.

The agent notes that Tamsin has settled the invoices, and asks whether the export can be generated.

question.instructions: Is Tamsin Reid still entitled to the data export under the policy as amended?

criteria.true: The export request falls within the window that applies and meets its conditions.
criteria.false: The export request falls outside the window that applies or fails a condition.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: Termination is the final suspension notice on 1 September. The account was terminated for non-payment, so section 2 applies rather than the 30-day rule, and Amendment DR-2 shortens that window to 7 days because termination was after 15 August. The request on 12 September is 11 days after termination, outside the window, even though the invoices are now settled.
provenance.why_hard: Settling the invoices satisfies the visible condition and 12 September is within both the 30-day and the 14-day windows; only the amended 7-day window excludes it.

state:
Returns processing note, Vantor Distribution, 20 September 2026, from the returns bench to the inventory controller.

A pair of "Aurel" wireless earbuds came back today under RMA 30-2291, reason "changed mind". The outer retail box has been opened and the cardboard sleeve is torn, but the inner clear seal around the earbuds and charging case is unbroken; the earbuds have plainly never been taken out. The bench operator needs to know the disposition code to enter.

The Returned Goods Disposition Procedure, issue 4, works as follows. The general rule in step 1 is that a returned item is inspected and, if it is resalable in as-new condition, is restocked as new; if it is complete and functional but shows signs of handling, it is restocked as open-box at a reduced price.

Step 2 is an exception for hygiene-sensitive items: a hygiene-sensitive item whose packaging has been opened is not restocked in any condition and is destroyed, because it cannot be resold. Step 2 originally allowed no other outcome for opened hygiene items.

Step 3 concerns recalled products, which are a separate case: any returned item that is subject to an active product recall is placed in quarantine for the manufacturer regardless of condition, and steps 1 and 2 do not apply. There is no active recall on the Aurel earbuds.

Step 4 gives definitions. "Hygiene-sensitive item" means an item on the hygiene list, which includes in-ear earbuds and headphones, razors, oral care products and swimwear. "Opened" means the outer retail packaging has been opened. "Inner seal" means a manufacturer's tamper-evident seal applied directly around the product inside the retail packaging. Step 4 also provides that where an amendment conflicts with steps 1 to 3, the amendment governs returns received on or after its effective date.

Amendment RGD-4.2, effective 1 June 2026, was introduced with the company's waste-reduction programme. It modifies step 2: an opened hygiene-sensitive item whose inner seal is intact and which shows no sign of use is donated to the approved charity partner instead of being destroyed. Such items are still not restocked in any condition. Opened hygiene items with a broken inner seal continue to be destroyed.

The controller is asked for the disposition.

question.instructions: What disposition should be recorded for the Aurel earbuds under the procedure as amended?

criteria.restock_as_new: Return the item to stock as new.
criteria.restock_as_open_box: Return the item to stock as open-box at a reduced price.
criteria.donate: Send the item to the approved charity partner.
criteria.quarantine: Place the item in quarantine for the manufacturer.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: In-ear earbuds are on the hygiene list and the outer retail packaging is opened, so step 2 applies and restocking in any condition is excluded. Amendment RGD-4.2 changes the outcome for opened hygiene items with an intact inner seal and no sign of use from destruction to donation; both conditions are met. There is no recall, so quarantine is out.
provenance.why_hard: The unbroken inner seal makes the item look perfectly resalable as open-box, but hygiene items are never restocked once the outer box is opened; the amendment only changes destroy to donate.

state:
IT Service Desk internal note, ticket HD-51877, prepared by the hardware coordinator for the desk lead.

Priya Anand, an account manager in the Commercial team, has asked for her laptop to be replaced. The device is a Corvex 14 issued on 20 January 2024, which makes it 32 months old at the time of the request. The hinge has failed and the screen no longer stays open. The authorised repairer has quoted 410 for the hinge and bezel repair. The current replacement value of a Corvex 14 on our standard catalogue is 1,050.

The Endpoint Hardware Standard, edition 3, governs replacement. Its base rule (section 4.1) is that a laptop becomes eligible for scheduled replacement once it has been in service for 36 months, measured from the issue date recorded in the asset register. Before 36 months the device is repaired rather than replaced.

Section 4.2 sets out an early-replacement exception: a device may be replaced before its scheduled date where the quoted cost of repair exceeds 50 percent of the current replacement value, or where the device has had two or more hardware repairs already recorded against it. The asset register shows no prior repairs for this device.

Section 4.5 concerns peripherals and is a separate matter: monitors, docks, keyboards and headsets are replaced on request when faulty, without reference to age, and are not subject to the 36-month cycle.

Section 2 gives definitions. A "field role" is a role listed in Appendix A of the Standard; the list is maintained by People Operations and is the only source used to determine field status. The appendix currently lists field service engineers, sales engineers and site auditors. Account managers are not listed, although the coordinator notes that several of them travel frequently.

Amendment 2 to the Standard, effective 1 July 2026, shortens the replacement cycle in section 4.1 from 36 months to 30 months for devices assigned to employees in field roles. It states that it does not alter section 4.2 and that, where it conflicts with the base text, the amendment applies.

The coordinator's question is whether the device qualifies for replacement now rather than repair.

question.instructions: Under the Endpoint Hardware Standard as amended, is Priya Anand's laptop eligible for replacement now?

criteria.true: The device meets a replacement condition under the Standard as amended.
criteria.false: The device meets no replacement condition and must be repaired.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: The 30-month cycle in Amendment 2 applies only to field roles, which Appendix A defines exhaustively; account managers are not listed, so the 36-month cycle applies and 32 months is short of it. The early-replacement exception needs a repair quote above 50 percent of replacement value; 410 is about 39 percent of 1,050, and there are no prior repairs. Neither route qualifies.
provenance.why_hard: The 30-month amendment and the frequent-travel remark make the device look eligible, but field status is determined only by the appendix list.

state:
Shift note from the receiving supervisor, Kestrel Distribution Centre, 22 September 2026, for the compliance lead.

A pallet arrived this morning from a new supplier containing 40 cartons of "Solvent Wipes Pro", a cleaning product. The safety data sheet classifies the contents as Class 3 flammable liquid. Each carton is a single sealed package with a net contents of 3 kg. The receiving clerk put the pallet on hold in the dock area and asked whether it can go to Zone C, which is our general ambient storage, because Zone H, the hazardous store, is nearly full this week.

The Hazardous Goods Storage Procedure, issue 6, sets the rule. Under paragraph 3.1, goods classified as dangerous under Classes 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 must be stored only in Zone H, which has the fire suppression and bunding required for them.

Paragraph 3.3 provides a limited-quantity exception: packages of dangerous goods where each individual package contains no more than 5 kg (or 5 litres) may be stored in general ambient zones, provided they are palletised, labelled and kept at least 3 metres from any exit. The exception exists for consumer-sized retail packs that would not sensibly be routed to the hazardous store.

Paragraph 3.5 deals with perishable and temperature-controlled goods, which are unrelated to this question: chilled and frozen goods go to Zone K regardless of any other classification, and the limited-quantity exception has no bearing on them.

Paragraph 2 defines terms. "Package" means the smallest sealed unit as received, so a carton received sealed is one package even if it contains smaller retail units inside. "Class" refers to the class stated on the supplier's safety data sheet. Paragraph 2 also says that where a later amendment sets a different threshold from paragraph 3.3, the amendment's threshold applies to the classes it names and paragraph 3.3 continues to apply to all other classes.

Amendment 6-2, issued 1 August 2026 following a fire risk assessment, reduces the limited-quantity threshold in paragraph 3.3 to 1 kg (or 1 litre) per package for Class 3 flammable liquids only. Other classes remain at 5 kg. The amendment applies to all goods received on or after its issue date.

The compliance lead is asked whether the pallet may be placed in Zone C.

question.instructions: Under the procedure as amended, may the Solvent Wipes Pro pallet be stored in Zone C?

criteria.true: The pallet falls within an exception that allows general ambient storage.
criteria.false: The pallet must go to Zone H and may not be stored in Zone C.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: The contents are Class 3, so paragraph 3.1 requires Zone H unless the limited-quantity exception applies. Amendment 6-2 lowers that exception's threshold to 1 kg per package for Class 3 only. Each sealed carton is one package under paragraph 2 and contains 3 kg, above 1 kg, so the exception is not available and Zone C is not permitted. Zone H being nearly full does not change the rule.
provenance.why_hard: At 3 kg the packages are comfortably under the 5 kg exception in the base text, and the exception was written for exactly this sort of consumer product; only the class-specific amendment removes it.

state:
Note from the support engineering liaison to the triage lead.

A support escalation has come in from Tavener & Holt, a mid-tier customer, about calendar invitations losing their time zone when forwarded from the mobile app. Support found ticket BUG-4418, which matches the customer's description exactly and was closed six weeks ago with the resolution "Duplicate of BUG-4390". BUG-4390 is open at priority P2 with 14 customer-impact entries and is scheduled for the release after next. The customer's account manager has asked triage to reopen BUG-4418 at P1 "so the customer can see their own ticket moving and we don't lose the renewal", and support would like to give the customer something concrete today.

Bug Tracker Rules (engineering handbook, section 9)
9.1 Reopening: a ticket closed as "Duplicate" is never reopened; new reports of the same defect are attached to the canonical open ticket named in the resolution. A ticket closed as "Won't fix" may be reopened only by the product owner.
9.2 Customer reports: each new customer report is recorded as a customer-impact entry on the canonical ticket, with the account name and any renewal risk noted. Priority of the canonical ticket is reviewed when the customer-impact count changes.
9.3 New tickets are opened only for defects with no existing open ticket after a search.
9.4 Customer-facing status is reported against the canonical ticket; support may share that ticket's reference and scheduled release with the customer.
9.5 Escalations to the product owner concern priority changes on open tickets, not reopening duplicates.

question.instructions: Using only the liaison note and the tracker rules, choose the action the triage lead should take.

criteria.reopen_bug_4418_as_p1: Reopen BUG-4418 at P1 so Tavener & Holt has its own ticket to follow.
criteria.open_new_ticket_for_customer: Open a fresh ticket for Tavener & Holt's report and set it to P1.
criteria.escalate_to_product_owner_to_reopen: Ask the product owner to reopen BUG-4418.
criteria.attach_report_to_bug_4390_and_share_refe: Record Tavener & Holt as a customer-impact entry on BUG-4390 with the renewal risk, trigger the priority review, and have support share BUG-4390's reference and schedule.
criteria.close_escalation_no_action: Tell support the defect is already known and take no further action.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-tradeoff
provenance.rationale: BUG-4418 was closed as a duplicate, and 9.1 says such tickets are never reopened; the product owner's reopen power covers only won't-fix (9.1, 9.5). A new ticket is barred by 9.3 because an open ticket exists. 9.2 requires recording the report on the canonical ticket BUG-4390 with the renewal risk and reviewing priority, and 9.4 lets support give the customer that reference, so 'no action' leaves required steps undone.
provenance.why_hard: Reopening gives the customer and account manager exactly what they asked for and looks like responsiveness during a renewal, while attaching to another ticket looks like a brush-off.

state:
Renewal pricing memo, Sable Forms (SaaS), 19 September 2026, from the renewals specialist to the billing manager.

Kestrel Learning Co-op renews on 1 November 2026. The account has been a paying customer since 1 May 2024, so at the coming renewal it will have completed two full contract years and be part-way through a third. The customer has never received a loyalty discount at any previous renewal. It is a co-operative that sells training courses commercially; it is not a registered charity or non-profit. The customer has asked whether a discount applies at this renewal.

The Renewal Pricing Policy, version 6, provides as follows. Section 1, the base rule: renewals are priced at the then-current list price for the plan.

Section 2, the loyalty exception: a customer with at least two completed contract years at the renewal date receives a 10 percent loyalty discount on the renewal invoice. A 15 percent tier was proposed in a draft but was never adopted; the policy notes that only the 10 percent rate exists.

Section 3, the non-profit programme, is a separate arrangement: registered charities and non-profits receive a 20 percent discount on all invoices on production of a registration certificate. Section 3 discounts do not stack with section 2.

Section 4, definitions: a "completed contract year" is a full twelve-month term that has been paid in full and has ended; the current term does not count until it ends. "Registered non-profit" means an entity holding a charity or non-profit registration number in its country of incorporation. Section 4 also provides that a later amendment displaces conflicting text in sections 1 to 3 for renewals dated on or after its effective date.

Amendment RP-6.1, effective 1 July 2026, raises the loyalty threshold in section 2 from two completed contract years to three. The amendment includes a grandfathering provision: any customer who has already received the loyalty discount at a previous renewal continues to receive it, regardless of the new threshold. Customers who have not yet received it must meet the three-year threshold.

The billing manager has asked what price the renewal invoice should carry.

question.instructions: What pricing applies to Kestrel Learning Co-op's 1 November 2026 renewal under the policy as amended?

criteria.list_price: The then-current list price with no discount.
criteria.loyalty_10_percent: List price less the 10 percent loyalty discount.
criteria.loyalty_15_percent: List price less a 15 percent loyalty discount.
criteria.nonprofit_20_percent: List price less the 20 percent non-profit discount.
criteria.negotiated_custom: A custom price negotiated by the account team.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: At 1 November 2026 the customer has two completed contract years; the third is in progress and does not count under section 4. Amendment RP-6.1 raises the threshold to three years for renewals after 1 July 2026, and the grandfathering clause does not help because the customer has never received the discount. The co-operative is not a registered non-profit, so section 3 is unavailable. List price applies.
provenance.why_hard: Two completed years meets the printed section 2 threshold exactly and the grandfathering language suggests leniency, but it protects only customers who already had the discount.

Work down the list and act on the first row that applies; lower rows do not apply while a higher row is open.
| Row | Condition | Permitted action |
| 1 | Fraud investigation open | No goods, refunds or credits. Refer to Risk. |
| 2 | Chargeback open on the order | No replacement, refund, exchange or credit may be issued on the disputed order until the bank closes the dispute, because the bank may also return the funds. Agent explains this to the customer and offers to expedite once the customer withdraws the dispute or the bank closes it. |
| 3 | Damage or defect reported within 30 days with photos | Replacement shipped at the customer's chosen speed at no charge; original item recalled with a prepaid label. |
| 4 | Courtesy credit | Up to $25 at agent discretion for service failures. |

Expense query raised by the finance assistant, 11 September 2026.

Noor Ibrahim, a regional trainer, has claimed mileage for a 212 km round trip on 5 September 2026 to deliver a session at the Westbridge depot. She drove her own car, which is registered in the fleet system as a plug-in hybrid: it has a battery good for about 50 km and a petrol engine for the rest. She claimed at the standard rate. The assistant is not sure whether the electric-vehicle rate should apply instead, and has asked for a ruling before the claim is paid.

The Business Travel Policy, part 5, sets the mileage rules. The base rule, 5.1, is that mileage in a private vehicle is reimbursed at 0.40 per kilometre, with the route distance taken from the company mapping tool.

Rule 5.2 is an exception for electric vehicles: mileage in a private electric vehicle is reimbursed at 0.30 per kilometre, the lower figure reflecting lower running costs. The policy notes that the employee must have registered the vehicle type in the fleet system before the journey.

Rule 5.4 covers public transport, which is a different category: rail, bus and taxi fares are reimbursed at actual cost against receipts, and no per-kilometre rate applies to them. A journey partly by car and partly by train is claimed under 5.1 or 5.2 for the driven part and under 5.4 for the rest.

Part 2, definitions: an "electric vehicle" for the purposes of 5.2 means a vehicle powered solely by a battery with no internal combustion engine. Plug-in hybrids and mild hybrids are treated as standard vehicles under 5.1. The definitions also state that where an amendment to part 5 conflicts with the printed text, the amendment applies to journeys made on or after its effective date.

Amendment BT-5.3, effective 1 August 2026, raises the electric-vehicle rate in 5.2 from 0.30 to 0.35 per kilometre, following a review of charging costs. The amendment explicitly leaves the standard rate in 5.1 and the definitions in part 2 unchanged.

The finance assistant has confirmed that the vehicle was registered as a plug-in hybrid in the fleet system in 2025 and that 212 km matches the mapping tool.

question.instructions: At what rate should Noor Ibrahim's 5 September mileage be reimbursed under the policy as amended?

criteria.rate_0_30: 0.30 per kilometre, the original electric-vehicle rate.
criteria.rate_0_35: 0.35 per kilometre, the amended electric-vehicle rate.
criteria.rate_0_40: 0.40 per kilometre, the standard private-vehicle rate.
criteria.actual_fuel_cost: Reimburse actual fuel receipts rather than a per-kilometre rate.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: Part 2 defines an electric vehicle as battery-only with no combustion engine and says plug-in hybrids are standard vehicles under 5.1. The amendment changes only the electric-vehicle rate, not the definition, so it does not reach a plug-in hybrid. The standard rate of 0.40 applies.
provenance.why_hard: A car with a plug and a battery looks electric, and the recent amendment draws attention to the electric rate, but the definitions paragraph excludes hybrids.

Dispatch planning memo, Corrigan Fresh Foods, 21 September 2026.

An order of 18 cartons of chilled cheese is due to leave the Halford depot today for a retailer in Bellmere. The dispatch clerk has asked which carrier service to book. The Bellmere postcode is in the carrier's zone 3, and the depot's service reach table shows that ground service from Halford reaches zone 3 in two days; zones 5 and above are beyond two-day ground reach. The cartons are packed in insulated liners. The clerk's instinct is to book overnight express to be safe, as the product is perishable.

The Outbound Carrier Selection Standard, version 2, sets the base rule in clause 1: domestic shipments are booked on standard ground service unless another clause requires otherwise.

Clause 2 is an exception for perishable goods: perishable shipments are booked on express overnight service, so that transit time is minimised.

Clause 3 concerns hazardous materials, which are a separate matter: any shipment containing dangerous goods must be booked with the approved hazmat courier regardless of destination or urgency, and clauses 1 and 2 do not apply to it. Chilled foods are not dangerous goods.

Clause 4 gives definitions: "perishable" means goods requiring temperature control during transit, including chilled and frozen foods; "within two-day ground reach" means a destination zone that the depot's current service reach table shows as reachable by ground service in two days or fewer from the dispatching depot. Clause 4 also provides that where an amendment conflicts with clauses 1 to 3, the amendment governs shipments dispatched on or after its effective date.

Amendment OCS-2.1, effective 1 July 2026, was issued after a cost review. It replaces clause 2 with a two-part rule: perishable shipments to destinations beyond two-day ground reach continue to be booked on express overnight service; perishable shipments to destinations within two-day ground reach are booked on ground service with gel ice packs added to each carton, since the insulated liners and ice packs maintain temperature for up to 72 hours. The amendment notes that express two-day service is not an approved option for perishables under either part, because it costs more than ground with ice packs without being materially faster than two-day ground.

The clerk needs the correct booking.

question.instructions: Which carrier service must be booked for the Bellmere cheese shipment under the standard as amended?

state:
Ticket REL-3310 (from release engineer, on-call)

The nightly build for 5.9 failed on integration tests overnight. Do I block tomorrow's release or not? The failing suite is payments-e2e, one test, "refund_partial_multi_tender", timed out at 120 s. I can't remember whether payments-e2e is on the flaky list; I know a couple of the payments suites were added to it in August after the sandbox latency issues, but I don't know if this was one of them. The repo is locked for the freeze so I can't open flaky.yaml, and the two people who'd know are both out until Thursday. Everything else is green.

--- Release gate rule (reference) ---
A failure in any release-gating suite blocks the release. Suites listed in flaky.yaml are not release-gating; a failure there is logged and the release proceeds. A suite is release-gating unless it is listed in flaky.yaml. There is no waiver process during a freeze.

question.instructions: Should the release be blocked on the basis of the payments-e2e failure?

criteria.block_release: Block the release; the failing suite is release-gating.
criteria.proceed_with_release: Proceed; the failing suite is not release-gating.
criteria.insufficient_information: This cannot be determined because the state does not establish whether payments-e2e is listed in flaky.yaml.
criteria.proceed_with_waiver: Proceed under a waiver for the single failing test.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: The rule makes the outcome depend entirely on whether payments-e2e is in flaky.yaml. The engineer does not know, cannot open the file, and only recalls that some payments suites were added. No fact in the ticket resolves the listing, and there is no waiver route during a freeze.
provenance.why_hard: The default that a suite is release-gating unless listed makes blocking feel like the safe reading, but the listing is exactly the unknown fact; the rule does not say to assume unlisted.

Internal note from the subscriptions team lead, 23 September 2026.

Tenant Corvane Studios (annual plan, renews 1 November) has emailed to cancel at the end of the current term and, in the same email, to have "all our data permanently deleted immediately, including backups" under their statutory right to erasure. The support agent handling it wants to run the deletion tool today so the customer sees that we respect privacy requests quickly, and to confirm the cancellation in the same reply.

Two facts are on the tenant record. First, General Counsel placed a legal hold on the Corvane tenant on 4 September 2026, in connection with a contract dispute between Corvane and one of its own clients; the hold notice lists the tenant ID and says "all tenant data and backups". Second, the tenant has an unpaid overage invoice of $310 from July, which the customer has not mentioned.

Data Handling Standard, section 7 — order of precedence for tenant lifecycle requests
7.1 Legal hold. A hold notice from General Counsel suspends every form of deletion for the named tenant, including deletion requested under statutory rights, until General Counsel lifts it in writing. The requester is told within 10 days that deletion is deferred and why, in general terms.
7.2 Statutory deletion requests are completed within 30 days of receipt, unless 7.1 applies.
7.3 A cancellation becomes effective when the paid term ends. It is processed on request and does not depend on deletion, payment status or any hold.
7.4 Default retention after a cancelled term is 90 days, after which data is deleted automatically unless 7.1 applies.
7.5 Unpaid balances are pursued under the Collections Handbook and do not block cancellation.

question.instructions: Using only the note and the standard, choose the action the subscriptions team should take on Corvane's email.

criteria.delete_all_data_and_backups_today: Run the deletion tool today and confirm both the deletion and the cancellation.
criteria.process_cancellation_defer_deletion_noti: Confirm the end-of-term cancellation, defer the deletion under the legal hold, tell the customer deletion is deferred, and notify General Counsel of the request.
criteria.refuse_cancellation_until_hold_lifted: Tell the customer the account cannot be cancelled while a legal hold is in place.
criteria.schedule_deletion_for_day_30: Confirm cancellation and schedule deletion for 30 days from now to use the full statutory window.
criteria.block_cancellation_until_overage_paid: Hold the cancellation until the $310 overage invoice is paid, then delete.

provenance.rationale: 7.1 suspends all deletion, including statutory requests, while the General Counsel hold stands, and requires the customer to be told it is deferred. 7.3 says cancellation is processed regardless of holds or payment status, and 7.5 says unpaid balances do not block it. provenance.why_hard: Acting immediately on an erasure request looks like the privacy-respecting thing, and the legal hold concerns a dispute the customer has with someone else.

Release management note, Corvina mobile app team, 16 September 2026, for the release captain.

Bug MOB-4180 has been proposed for inclusion in the hotfix train that ships tomorrow. The bug is that the in-app document scanner crops the top 15 percent of a page when the device is in landscape orientation. It was found by QA during the 4.3 regression pass. QA has verified that the same steps on build 4.2.6, the previous release, produce a correctly cropped image, and that on 4.3.0, the current production build, the crop is wrong. Triage has assigned the bug priority P2. No customer has raised it, and there is no committed fix date on any customer account.

The Hotfix Admission Policy, revision 2, governs what may ship in a hotfix. The base rule, in section 1, is that only defects with priority P1 are admitted to a hotfix train; everything else waits for the next scheduled release.

Section 2 provides an exception: a P2 defect may be admitted where a customer has been given a committed fix date in writing by the account team and that date falls before the next scheduled release. The exception requires the account team to attach the commitment to the ticket.

Section 3 concerns feature requests and small enhancements, which are a different category: they are never admitted to a hotfix train, even where a customer has a commitment, and are handled through the roadmap process instead.

Section 4 gives definitions. "Regression" means a defect where the affected behaviour worked correctly in the immediately preceding production release and QA has recorded the comparison in the ticket. A defect that has existed across several releases is not a regression even if it was only recently noticed. "Current release" means the build presently in production.

Section 5 says that later amendments prevail over sections 1 to 3 where they conflict.

Amendment R2-1, effective 1 September 2026, adds a second exception: a P2 defect is admitted to a hotfix train if it is a regression, as defined in section 4, introduced in the current release. The amendment does not require a customer commitment for this route and states that section 2 continues to apply unchanged for non-regression P2 defects.

The release captain wants to know whether MOB-4180 can be admitted to tomorrow's hotfix.

question.instructions: Under the Hotfix Admission Policy as amended, may MOB-4180 be admitted to the hotfix train?

criteria.true: The defect satisfies an admission route under the policy.
criteria.false: The defect satisfies no admission route under the policy.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: MOB-4180 is P2, so section 1 alone would exclude it, and there is no customer commitment for section 2. But QA recorded that the behaviour worked in 4.2.6 and broke in 4.3.0, the current production build, which makes it a regression introduced in the current release under section 4. Amendment R2-1 admits such P2 regressions without a commitment.
provenance.why_hard: The absence of any customer commitment makes the only visible exception fail, and the regression route lives in an amendment paragraph after the definitions.

state.request: Write a JavaScript function daysInMonth(year, month) where month is 1 to 12, returning the number of days in that month.

question.instructions: Read the request and the response. Decide whether the response fully and correctly satisfies the request, including every explicit constraint.

criteria.true: The response is complete and correct for the request as stated, even if terse or unusually formatted.
criteria.false: The response contains an error, misses an explicit constraint, or fails to satisfy some part of the request.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-adequacy
provenance.rationale: In the JavaScript Date constructor months are 0-based and day 0 gives the last day of the previous month. new Date(year, month - 1, 0) therefore returns the length of month − 1: daysInMonth(2026, 3) returns 28 (February) instead of 31. The correct call is new Date(year, month, 0).
provenance.why_hard: The day-0 trick is a well-known idiom and subtracting 1 from a 1-based month is what one normally does with Date.

state.request: Write a Python function inclusive_range(a, b) that returns a list of the integers from a to b inclusive, assuming a <= b.
state.response:
def inclusive_range(a, b):
    return list(range(a, b))

question.instructions: Read the request and the response. Decide whether the response fully and correctly satisfies the request, including every explicit constraint.

criteria.true: The response is complete and correct for the request as stated, even if terse or unusually formatted.
criteria.false: The response contains an error, misses an explicit constraint, or fails to satisfy some part of the request.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-adequacy
provenance.rationale: range(a, b) stops before b, so inclusive_range(1, 3) returns [1, 2] and omits the endpoint. The request explicitly requires b to be included; range(a, b + 1) was needed.
provenance.why_hard: The function is idiomatic and returns the right start and length-minus-one, so only checking the last element reveals the off-by-one.

state:
Summary written by the helpdesk analyst on ticket 60218.

Priya Nandakumar, a sales operations analyst who works from the Dunmore regional office, reports that her laptop battery now lasts about 25 minutes off the charger. The laptop works normally when plugged in. She has a two-day customer site visit starting Thursday, where she says power sockets are scarce, and asks for a new laptop shipped overnight "so I'm not stranded". She is not a member of field or sales staff under the asset register; her role is classed as office-based. The analyst notes that the Dunmore office keeps a loaner pool of four laptops, of which two are currently available, and that a replacement laptop from central stock takes three business days by standard shipping.

Hardware Support Standard, section 5 (extract)
5.1 Priority definitions for hardware tickets: P1, a failure that stops a business service for many users; P2, a hardware failure that prevents a user from doing any work, or any hardware fault for staff classed as field-based; P3, a fault that degrades work but leaves the device usable; P4, cosmetic or preference requests.
5.2 Shipping: expedited (overnight) shipping of replacement hardware is used only for P1 and P2 tickets. P3 and P4 replacements are sent by standard shipping.
5.3 Loaners: where a P3 ticket involves travel or a known period away from the office, the analyst arranges a loaner from the nearest regional pool for the period of the standard shipment.
5.4 Personal purchase of replacement parts or devices for later expense claim is not permitted; hardware is supplied only through the helpdesk.
5.5 Priority is set by 5.1 alone and is not raised on request; a ticket may be re-prioritised only if the reported facts change.

question.instructions: Using only the ticket summary and the standard, choose the action the analyst should take.

criteria.overnight_ship_replacement_laptop: Order a replacement laptop with overnight shipping so it arrives before Thursday.
criteria.standard_ship_replacement_no_loaner: Order a replacement by standard shipping and tell Priya to charge frequently until it arrives.
criteria.raise_ticket_to_p2_and_expedite: Re-prioritise the ticket to P2 because of the travel and expedite shipping.
criteria.issue_loaner_and_standard_ship_replaceme: Arrange a loaner from the Dunmore pool for the trip and order a replacement by standard shipping.
criteria.advise_buying_battery_and_expensing: Suggest she buy a replacement battery locally and claim it on expenses.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-tradeoff
provenance.rationale: The fault degrades work but the device is usable, and Priya is office-based, so the ticket is P3 under 5.1; 5.2 restricts expedited shipping to P1 and P2, and 5.5 forbids raising priority on request. 5.3 directs the analyst to arrange a loaner for the travel period alongside the standard shipment. 5.4 rules out an expensed purchase.
provenance.why_hard: The user has a genuine trip in two days and an overnight shipment is the direct way to make sure she is not stranded, so it looks like the caring choice.

The temperature logger on the Merrow Foods trailer that just docked shows a spike to 9 C for about 40 minutes around 03:00, then back down to 3 C for the rest of the run. A load is rejected if any product line on the manifest was exposed to a temperature above its maximum for longer than 15 minutes. Maximum transit temperature: dairy lines 8 C; packaged produce lines 10 C. Lines are assessed individually against the logger record; a load with only some lines exceeding their maximum is accepted with those lines rejected.

C. Marchetti has asked the manager to find a way, noting that she is the most senior member, that the wedding date cannot move, and that B. Ilunga "could probably go another week". The manager would like to help.

Leave Policy, section 11 — Conflicting requests and staffing minimums
11.1 Precedence when requests conflict with the staffing minimum, highest first:
   (a) statutory absences (jury service, statutory parental leave) - the company may not refuse or ask the employee to defer them;
   (b) leave already approved - may be rescinded only for a declared business emergency (regulatory inspection, major system outage) and never to accommodate another leave request;
   (c) pending requests, in order of submission date; seniority is used only to break ties between requests submitted on the same day.
11.2 A pending request that would breach the staffing minimum is declined for those dates, and the manager offers the nearest dates on which it can be approved. A manager may not approve a request that breaches the minimum.
11.3 The manager decides pending requests within five working days. The HR business partner is involved only for grievances or where the manager is the requester.

criteria.approve_marchetti_and_ask_fenwick_to_def: Approve C. Marchetti and ask A. Fenwick to request a deferral of jury service.
criteria.decline_marchetti_and_offer_alternative_: Decline the 12-16 October request under the staffing minimum and offer the nearest approvable dates.
criteria.approve_all_three_run_below_minimum: Approve C. Marchetti and run the week with one member present.
criteria.escalate_to_hr_business_partner: Refer the conflict to the HR business partner to decide.

--- IDENTITY VERIFICATION STANDARD, extract (v3) ---

V1. Standard verification
V1.1 Before resetting a user's password, the service desk verifies identity by calling the user back on the phone number registered in the directory and confirming two profile details.

V2. No registered phone
V2.1 Where the user has no registered phone number, or the number is unreachable, the user's line manager confirms the user's identity in person or by a call from the manager's own registered number. Manager confirmation under V2 replaces the callback.

V3. Service accounts (neighbouring case type)
V3.1 Service and shared accounts have no individual owner. Password rotation for these accounts follows the Service Account Procedure and is never performed through a desk reset request. V1 and V2 do not apply to service accounts.

For privileged accounts, verification requires both the callback under V1.1 and manager confirmation as described in V2.1, regardless of whether a registered phone exists. Neither method alone is sufficient for a privileged account. Non-privileged accounts continue under V1 and V2 unchanged.

One unit of the Aster stand mixer (sage colour) remains in stock, and the next delivery from the supplier is six weeks away. Three demands are waiting on it.

The second is pre-order K-11740, placed on 2 August when the sage colour was announced; it is the earliest pre-order for this variant still unfilled.

The third is a marketplace order received through the Vendora channel on Saturday. Vendora's terms impose a $50 late-shipment penalty and a seller-score deduction if the order is not dispatched within two business days, and the marketplace coordinator has asked that the unit go there, adding that "the other two customers have already waited, another six weeks won't change much for them, but a penalty and a score hit will hurt us".

Allocation Policy (operations manual, section 12)
When a unit is scarce, allocate in this order and do not skip a tier while any demand in it is unfilled:
Tier 1: replacements for items confirmed defective by the returns team.
Tier 2: pre-orders, earliest order timestamp first.
Tier 3: marketplace channel orders.
Tier 4: standard website orders.
Notes: marketplace penalties and seller-score effects are a Tier 3 cost and do not raise a marketplace order to a higher tier. Order value does not affect tier. Customers whose orders are not filled are told the new expected date within one business day.

state:
Sales operations note, Quillstack (SaaS), 24 September 2026.

An account executive has asked what she can offer a trial customer, Ferrow Design Studio. The studio started a 14-day trial on 27 August 2026. On 9 September, the day before it expired, the executive extended it under the sales-qualified route, and that extension ends today. The studio has an opportunity record in the CRM, opened on 3 September with a forecast close in October. They now say they need "another couple of weeks" to finish evaluating and have asked for a second extension. The executive would like to grant it.

The Trial Policy, version 4, provides as follows. Section 1, the base rule: trials last 14 days and are not extended; at the end of the trial the workspace is locked until a paid plan is chosen.

Section 2, the sales-qualified exception: where a trial account has an associated opportunity record in the CRM, the account executive may extend the trial by a further 14 days. The printed text placed no limit on the number of extensions.

Section 3 covers the free tier, a separate mechanism: a trial account that does not convert may be downgraded to the free tier on the customer's request, which retains their data with reduced limits. Section 3 does not extend the trial and does not require an opportunity record.

Section 4, definitions: "sales-qualified" means a trial account with an opportunity record in the CRM at the time the extension is requested; "extension" means any lengthening of the trial beyond the original 14 days, however granted. Section 4 also provides that later amendments displace conflicting text in sections 1 to 3 for extensions requested on or after their effective date.

Amendment TP-4.1, effective 1 August 2026, changes section 2 in two respects: the extension period is reduced from 14 days to 7 days, and only one extension may be granted per trial account, by the account executive, with no escalation route for a second. The amendment states that a trial that has already been extended once is at the end of its permitted life when that extension expires, and the customer may then convert or use section 3.

The executive wants to know what she may do.

question.instructions: What may the account executive offer Ferrow Design Studio under the policy as amended?

criteria.extend_14_days: Extend the trial by a further 14 days under section 2.
criteria.extend_7_days: Extend the trial by a further 7 days under the amended section 2.
criteria.escalate_to_sales_director: Escalate to the sales director for approval of a second extension.
criteria.no_further_extension: No further extension; the customer must convert or request the free tier.
criteria.downgrade_to_free_automatically: The account is downgraded to the free tier automatically.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: The trial has already been extended once, on 9 September, after Amendment TP-4.1 took effect. The amendment allows only one extension per trial account and expressly provides no escalation route for a second. Section 3's free tier is available only on the customer's request, so it is not automatic. The executive cannot extend again.
provenance.why_hard: The account is sales-qualified and the amendment still allows a 7-day extension, so a shorter second extension seems like the compromise; the one-extension cap in the same amendment forbids it.

Service desk memo, 15 September 2026, from the queue lead to the desk manager regarding ticket HD-60392.

The requester, Ivo Marchetti, asked this morning (Monday 14 September 2026) for ticket HD-60392 to be reopened. The ticket concerned his VPN client failing with error code VPN-118 after a laptop image refresh. It was resolved by reinstalling the client and closed on Tuesday 1 September 2026. He now reports that the VPN is failing again, this time with error code VPN-207, which the knowledge base describes as a certificate expiry error, and he would prefer the old ticket reopened so the history stays together rather than a new one raised.

The Ticket Lifecycle Standard, version 4, sets the rules. The base rule in 5.1 is that a resolved ticket closes automatically after five business days without a response from the requester, and a closed ticket may be reopened by the requester within ten business days of the closure date. After that, a new ticket must be raised.

Clause 5.2 provides an exception for recurrence: a closed ticket may be reopened at any time, without regard to the ten-day window, where the same fault recurs. The clause defines "same fault" as the same error code or the same knowledge-base article reference as recorded on the original ticket.

Clause 5.4 concerns priority escalation, a different process: a requester who believes an open ticket is under-prioritised may ask for escalation, which is reviewed by the queue lead within one business day. Escalation does not reopen closed tickets and has its own form.

Clause 2, definitions, states that "business days" are Monday to Friday excluding the company holidays listed in the annual calendar. The 2026 calendar lists Monday 7 September 2026 as a company holiday. The clause also provides that where an amendment changes a number in clause 5, the amended number applies to closures occurring on or after the amendment's effective date.

Amendment TLS-4.1, effective 1 August 2026, reduces the reopen window in clause 5.1 from ten business days to seven business days. The amendment states that clause 5.2 is unchanged.

The queue lead counts the business days between the closure and the request and asks whether the reopen is permitted.

question.instructions: Under the Ticket Lifecycle Standard as amended, may ticket HD-60392 be reopened?

criteria.true: The reopen falls within the applicable window or an exception permits it.
criteria.false: The reopen falls outside the applicable window and no exception applies.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: The closure was 1 September, after the amendment, so the window is seven business days. Excluding the weekend days and the 7 September holiday, the business days after closure are 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11 September (seven) and 14 September is the eighth, outside the window. The recurrence exception needs the same error code; VPN-118 and VPN-207 differ, so 5.2 does not apply.
provenance.why_hard: Under the original ten-day window the reopen is clearly in time, and the fault feels like a recurrence of the same VPN problem, but the amended window and the error-code definition both cut against it.

--- MERIDIAN PARCEL CLAIMS TERMS (Business tier), extract ---

C1. Damage claims
C1.1 A claim for damage in transit must be submitted within 7 calendar days of the delivery date.
C1.2 Photographs of the goods and packaging must accompany the claim.

C2. High-value consignments
C2.1 Where the declared value exceeds 500.00, a damage claim must additionally be supported by a carrier inspection report, and the inspection must be requested within 14 calendar days of delivery. Claims under C2 are assessed by the Cargo Loss team.

C3. Lost consignments (separate procedure)
C3.1 A claim that a consignment was not delivered must be submitted within 21 calendar days of the expected delivery date shown on the tracking page. Photographs are not required. C1 does not apply to lost-consignment claims.

C4. Definitions and precedence
C4.1 "Delivery date" means the date of the carrier's proof-of-delivery scan.
C4.2 "Submitted" means the time stamp on a claim ticket opened in the Meridian claims portal. Emails, phone calls or messages to account managers do not constitute submission, although they may be attached to a portal ticket as evidence.
C4.3 Where a later amendment conflicts with C1 to C3, the amendment governs claims whose delivery date falls on or after the amendment's effective date.

--- AMENDMENT CT-9 (effective 1 August 2026) ---
The submission period in C1.1 is extended from 7 to 10 calendar days for claims submitted through the claims portal. Claims submitted by any other route remain subject to C1.1 as originally drafted and, by virtue of C4.2, are not treated as submitted.

state:
Equipment desk note, 23 September 2026, from the desk analyst to the desk lead.

A request has come in from Priyanka Sethi, an external contractor engaged through a consultancy for a data migration project. She will be working on site at the Harrowgate client facility for the next two months and has asked for a company laptop for 60 days, explaining that the client site does not allow personal devices onto its network. Her engagement record is in order and her engagement manager has approved the request in the ticket. There is no note from the security team on the ticket.

The Contractor Equipment Policy, version 3, has the following structure. The base rule in section 1 is that contractors are not issued company hardware; they work on their own devices under the bring-your-own-device standard, with access provided through the virtual desktop.

Section 2 is an exception: a contractor who must work at a client site listed in Schedule 1 as requiring managed devices may be issued a laptop from the loaner pool for the duration of the on-site work. Schedule 1 currently lists the Harrowgate facility, the Northlake plant and the Merrow data centre.

Section 3 concerns interns and is a different case: interns are employees for equipment purposes and are issued a standard laptop from stock on their start date without any of the conditions in sections 1 or 2.

Section 4, definitions: "loaner pool" means the pool of pre-imaged laptops held by the equipment desk for temporary issue; "client site" means a location listed in Schedule 1; "engagement manager" means the employee named on the contractor's engagement record. Section 4 also states that where an amendment conflicts with sections 1 to 3, the amendment governs requests raised on or after its effective date.

Amendment CE-3.1, effective 1 September 2026, tightens section 2 in two ways. First, a loaner under section 2 may be issued only after the security team has approved the request in the ticket, in addition to the engagement manager's approval. Second, the maximum period for a single loaner issue is 90 days; longer on-site work requires a fresh request. The amendment says that requests lacking security approval are held, not refused, until approval is recorded.

The analyst asks what to do with the request.

question.instructions: How should the equipment desk handle Priyanka Sethi's request under the policy as amended?

criteria.issue_loaner_now: Issue a loaner pool laptop for 60 days immediately.
criteria.issue_standard_laptop: Issue a standard laptop from stock as for a new starter.
criteria.deny_byod_only: Refuse the request; contractors use their own devices.
criteria.hold_pending_security_approval: Hold the request until the security team approves it in the ticket.
criteria.escalate_to_procurement: Escalate to procurement to purchase a new device.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: Harrowgate is a Schedule 1 site and the engagement manager has approved, so the section 2 exception is engaged and a flat refusal is wrong. But Amendment CE-3.1, in force for requests after 1 September, requires security team approval in the ticket before a loaner is issued and says such requests are held until it is recorded. 60 days is within the 90-day limit, so duration is not an issue.
provenance.why_hard: Every visible condition of the section 2 exception is met and the manager has approved, so issuing now seems right; the extra security approval exists only in the amendment.

--- Parental leave rule (HR reference) ---
Paid parental leave: available where the employee has at least 12 months of continuous service on the day the leave starts. Unpaid parental leave: available where the employee has at least 6 months of continuous service on the day the leave starts. Employees with less than 6 months are not eligible for either. Service is measured from the start date on the offer letter.

T1. On-time delivery
T1.1 A next-day consignment is on time if the proof-of-delivery scan occurs by 17:00 on the promised delivery date.
T1.2 A consignment delivered late earns the shipper an on-time credit equal to the base shipping charge.

T2. Signature-required consignments
T2.1 For signature-required consignments, the first delivery attempt recorded by the driver counts as the delivery event for T1, even if the recipient is absent and the parcel is carded.

T3. Rural zones (neighbouring case type)
T3.1 Consignments to rural zone codes (prefix R) carry a two-day service standard instead of next-day, and T1.1 applies to the second day. No on-time credit is payable for rural consignments delivered by 17:00 on the second day.

T4. Definitions and precedence
T4.1 Zone codes are assigned from the delivery postcode at label creation. Codes with prefix M are metro zones; codes with prefix S are suburban zones; codes with prefix R are rural zones.
T4.2 "Proof-of-delivery scan" means the driver's handheld scan at the delivery point.
T4.3 Where a later amendment conflicts with T1 to T3, the amendment governs consignments with a promised delivery date on or after the amendment's effective date.

For consignments addressed to metro zones (prefix M), the cutoff in T1.1 is extended from 17:00 to 19:00 to reflect extended evening delivery rounds in metro areas. Suburban and rural cutoffs are unchanged.

--- APPLICABLE POLICY EXTRACT: RETURNS AND REFUNDS, version 7 ---

Section 1. Standard return window
1.1 A customer may return an item for a full refund to the original payment method if the return request is lodged within 30 days of the delivery date.
1.2 Items must be unused and in original packaging.

Section 2. Final-sale items
2.1 Items designated Clearance are final sale and may not be returned for refund, exchange or store credit, except where the item arrived damaged (see Section 4).

Section 3. Definitions
3.1 "Delivery date" means the date of the carrier's delivery scan, not the order date and not the dispatch date.
3.2 "Clearance" means an item carrying the tag "Clearance - Final Sale" at checkout. Items discounted under a promotional event (for example a percentage-off event tag) are not Clearance items and are governed by Section 1.
3.3 "Plus member" means a customer whose Larkfield Plus membership is active on the date the return request is lodged.

Section 4. Damaged or defective items (neighbouring case type)
4.1 Where an item arrives damaged or develops a defect, the customer may request an exchange within 60 days of the delivery date regardless of tier. Exchanges under this section are not refunds and are handled by the Quality desk, not the Returns desk.

Section 5. Precedence
5.1 Where a later amendment conflicts with a numbered section above, the amendment governs for any request lodged on or after the amendment's effective date.

--- AMENDMENT A-2026-08 (effective 1 August 2026) ---
For Plus members, the period in clause 1.1 is changed from 30 days to 45 days of the delivery date. This amendment applies to any return request lodged on or after 1 August 2026, regardless of when the order was placed or delivered. All other conditions of Section 1 continue to apply.

Escalation summary written by a returns team lead for the agent handling case RT-30371.

The customer, Mr. Adeyemi, returned a pair of noise-cancelling headphones ($340) within the return window. The item passed inspection and a refund is due. He has asked, politely but firmly, that the refund go to a different credit card, because the card he paid with was cancelled after a fraud alert last month and he says "the money will just vanish". He has offered to send a photo of the new card and his driving licence. He also mentions he is "not interested in store credit" because he does not plan to shop with us again.

The agent is inclined to help by refunding to the new card, since the customer has been reasonable and the old card no longer exists.

Refund Standard, section 5 (extract), applied in this order:
5.1 Every refund is returned to the payment instrument used for the original purchase. This applies even where the customer reports the card as lost, cancelled or replaced: card networks route a refund on a closed card to the cardholder through the issuing bank, and the agent informs the customer of this.
5.2 A refund may go to a different instrument only where the original instrument was a gift card that has since been fully redeemed, in which case the refund is issued as a new gift card.
5.3 Store credit is offered as an alternative only when the customer requests it in writing; it is never applied without the customer's request.
5.4 Identity verification (documents) is required for refunds of $1,000 or more.
5.5 Finance review is required when the original instrument was a bank transfer or where the refund exceeds $2,500.
Where sections appear to conflict, the lower-numbered section controls.

question.instructions: Using only the escalation summary and the refund standard, choose what the agent should do.

criteria.refund_to_customer_new_card: Refund $340 to the new card after the customer sends his card photo and licence.
criteria.refund_to_original_card_and_explain_rero: Refund $340 to the original card and explain that the issuing bank will route it to him.
criteria.issue_store_credit: Issue $340 store credit so the customer has immediate access to the funds.
criteria.hold_refund_for_identity_check: Hold the refund until documents are verified, then refund to the new card.
criteria.escalate_to_finance: Refer the case to Finance to decide the refund route.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-tradeoff
provenance.rationale: 5.1 controls: refunds go to the original instrument even when the card is cancelled, and the agent explains the rerouting by the issuing bank. 5.2 does not apply (the original instrument was a credit card, not a gift card). Store credit is barred by 5.3 because the customer has declined it. Identity checks (5.4) and finance review (5.5) are triggered by thresholds and instruments not present here.
provenance.why_hard: The customer's fear that the money will vanish sounds real and he offers verification, so paying the new card feels like the accommodating and safe thing.
