K1.1 An account with an invoice more than 15 days past due is suspended until payment is received. Reminders are sent at 3, 7 and 12 days past due.

K2. Enterprise exception
K2.1 An Enterprise tier account with a valid purchase order on file is not suspended until an invoice is more than 45 days past due.

K3. Trial and free accounts (neighbouring case type)
K3.1 Trial accounts that do not convert are downgraded to the free tier at the end of the trial; no collections action applies. K1 and K2 do not apply to free-tier accounts.

K4. Definitions and precedence
K4.1 "Days past due" is counted from the invoice due date, not from the invoice issue date.
K4.2 "Suspended" means all users are blocked from signing in until the balance is cleared.
K4.3 "Read-only mode" means users may sign in and view data but may not create, edit or export.
K4.4 Where an amendment conflicts with K1 to K3, the amendment governs invoices whose due date falls on or after its effective date.

For Enterprise tier accounts with a valid purchase order on file, the suspension in K2.1 is replaced by a two-stage ladder: the account is placed in read-only mode once an invoice is more than 45 days past due, and is fully suspended once the invoice is more than 75 days past due. Order Risk Ladder (fraud operations procedure, section 2)
| Score band | Classification | Required action |
| 0-39 | Low | Release to fulfilment. |
| 40-70 | Medium | Release only if 3-D Secure authentication succeeded on the payment. Otherwise hold for manual review by the fraud analyst, to be completed within 24 hours; the customer is told the order is delayed for a routine check, and any paid delivery upgrade is refunded if the promised slot is missed. |
| 71-100 | High | Cancel and refund; do not contact the customer for verification. |
Additional rules:
2.4 Verification by phone, email or customer-supplied documents is not a substitute for manual review and does not change the band.
2.5 Delivery speed, order value and customer stated urgency do not change the band or the required action.
2.6 Analysts may not downgrade a delivery option in lieu of review.
Fraud analyst availability: next review slot 14:30 today.

question.instructions: Using only the order risk review and the ladder, choose the action the agent should take on order H-77204.

criteria.release_for_same_day_dispatch: Release the order now so it makes the 13:00 same-day cutoff.
criteria.hold_for_manual_review_and_notify_delay: Hold the order for the analyst's review, tell the customer it is delayed for a routine check, and refund the same-day upgrade if the slot is missed.
criteria.cancel_order_and_refund: Cancel the order and refund the customer.
criteria.release_after_phone_confirmation: Call the customer on the number provided, confirm the order details, then release for same-day dispatch.
criteria.downgrade_to_standard_shipping_and_relea: Refund the same-day upgrade, switch to standard shipping and release the order.

state:
Refund desk note, Marlow & Finch Homeware, 17 September 2026.

A return has been approved today for order 1188420, a set of dining chairs. The order was placed on 20 April 2026, so it is 150 days old at approval. The customer, who did not use a gift receipt and is buying for herself, has told us that her bank issued her a new debit card in July after the old one was reported worn out; the card number changed but the underlying current account is the same and remains open. She has asked how the refund will reach her.

The Refund Method Policy, version 5, provides the answer. The general rule in section 1 is that refunds are returned to the original payment method used for the order, and that a refund to a card is credited to the account behind that card even if the card has since been reissued with a new number, because the card network routes it by account.

Section 2 is the exception for unusable payment methods: where the original card has expired and the account behind it has been closed, or where the payment method no longer exists (for example a closed digital wallet), the refund is issued as store credit to the customer's account. Section 2 states that store credit is used only where a refund to the original method would fail.

Section 3 addresses gift-receipt returns, which follow a different rule: where the item was bought with a gift receipt and returned by the recipient, the refund is issued as a gift card to the recipient, never to the purchaser's card, and sections 1 and 2 do not apply.

Section 4, definitions: "order age" is measured from the order date to the date the refund is approved by the returns desk. "Closed" means the bank or wallet provider has confirmed the account no longer exists; a card reissued with a new number on an open account is not closed. Section 4 also provides that a later amendment displaces sections 1 to 3 where they conflict.

Amendment RM-5.1, effective 1 March 2026, adds a rule for old orders: where the order age at refund approval exceeds 180 days, the refund is issued as store credit regardless of the state of the original payment method, because the payment processor no longer supports refunds against such transactions. Orders at or below 180 days are unaffected.

The desk agent has asked which method to use.

question.instructions: By which method should the refund for order 1188420 be issued under the policy as amended?

criteria.store_credit: Credit to the customer's store account.
criteria.original_payment_method: Refund to the card account used to pay for the order.
criteria.gift_card_to_recipient: A gift card issued to the person returning the item.
criteria.bank_transfer: A manual bank transfer to an account the customer nominates.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: The order is 150 days old at approval, below the 180-day threshold in Amendment RM-5.1, so the amendment does not force store credit. The card was reissued with a new number but the account is open, which section 4 says is not closed, so the section 2 exception does not apply. Section 1 governs and the refund routes to the original card account. Section 3 is irrelevant because no gift receipt was used.
provenance.why_hard: A replaced card and an old order both point toward store credit, but the order is under the amendment's threshold and the definitions say a reissued card on an open account is still usable.

The Service Level Agreement, version 3, provides as follows.

Clause 2, the uptime commitment: for the Business tier, monthly availability is committed at 99.9 percent. Where availability in a calendar month falls below the commitment, the customer is entitled to a credit of 10 percent of that month's fee on request. Clause 2 also states that the Enterprise tier commitment is 99.95 percent with a 25 percent credit; that tier is not relevant to Farrow, which has never been on it.

Clause 3, exclusions: downtime during scheduled maintenance is excluded from the availability calculation provided the maintenance was announced at least 72 hours in advance. Downtime caused by the customer's own network or by a third-party provider named in the customer's order form is also excluded.

Clause 5, definitions: "announced" means a post on the public status page; emails to account contacts do not count as an announcement for the purposes of clause 3. "Availability" is the percentage of minutes in the calendar month during which the service was reachable, after excluded minutes are removed from both numerator and denominator.

Clause 7, precedence: where an amendment published after this version conflicts with any clause, the amendment governs from its effective date for all customers on the affected tier.

Amendment SLA-3A, effective 1 September 2026, applies to the Business tier only. It changes the advance-notice requirement in clause 3 from 72 hours to 5 days (120 hours). The stated reason is that Business customers requested longer planning lead time. No other clause is changed.

The account manager's initial view, before reading the amendment, was that the 90 minutes of maintenance were excluded and that the 20 unplanned minutes alone would leave availability above 99.9 percent.

question.instructions: Is Farrow Logistics entitled to the September service credit under the SLA as amended?

criteria.true: September availability falls below the commitment that applies, so the credit is due.
criteria.false: September availability meets the commitment that applies, so no credit is due.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: Amendment SLA-3A requires 120 hours of status-page notice for Business tier maintenance to be excluded; the 21 September window was announced 96 hours ahead, so its 90 minutes count as downtime. Total downtime is 110 minutes out of 43,200, giving availability of about 99.75 percent, below the 99.9 percent commitment. The credit is due.
provenance.why_hard: Under the original 72-hour rule the maintenance would be excluded and only 20 minutes would count, which comfortably meets 99.9 percent; the amended notice period is the only thing that changes the outcome.

G1. Severity levels
G1.1 S1: a defect that causes loss or corruption of stored data.

state:
Evening shift note, Northgate chilled fulfilment centre, written by the shift lead at 20:55.

The 21:30 carrier departure is the last one tonight. Two pallets are on the outbound dock. Pallet P-4471 is a mixed chilled dairy order for Marren Foods, one of our three priority accounts, due at their depot by 07:00 tomorrow. Marren has had two late deliveries this month already and their buyer has phoned twice this evening; our account manager has asked that "whatever happens, Marren goes tonight". Pallet P-4483 is a chilled order for Bexley Deli, a standard account, which should have gone out yesterday and is now a day past its promised delivery date because of a picking error. The truck has room for both.

At 19:10 the staging-area data logger for P-4471 recorded 9.2 C for 47 minutes before the chiller door was found ajar. The product limit is 5 C. The pallet was moved back into the cold store at 19:57 and its current temperature is 3.8 C. The single data logger covers the whole pallet, so there is no per-case reading. The QA officer left at 20:00; the on-call QA officer has been paged and typically calls back within two to three hours.

Dispatch Standing Order 14 (extract), which governs loading decisions:
Priority of actions when goods compete for a departure, highest first:
1. Product-safety holds. Any pallet with a logged temperature excursion above the product limit is placed in quarantine and may not be loaded until QA releases it in writing. Delivery commitments, account status and carrier timing do not override this step.
2. Recall pulls instructed by Quality.
3. Orders already past their promised delivery date.
4. Priority-account orders still within their promised date.
5. All other orders.
Carrier departures are not held for pending QA releases; a pallet released after the departure goes on the next scheduled departure.
Where a pallet is quarantined, the shift lead notifies the account manager and QA, and the customer service desk contacts the customer the next morning.

question.instructions: Using only the shift note and the standing order, choose the action the shift lead should take for the 21:30 departure.

criteria.load_both_pallets_tonight: Load P-4471 and P-4483 on the 21:30 truck so both customers receive goods tomorrow.
criteria.load_marren_pallet_only: Load P-4471 for Marren and leave P-4483 for the next departure.
criteria.quarantine_marren_pallet_and_load_bexley: Place P-4471 in quarantine pending QA release and load only P-4483 on the 21:30 truck.
criteria.hold_truck_until_qa_calls_back: Ask the carrier to wait until the on-call QA officer releases P-4471, then load both.
criteria.ship_unaffected_cases_from_marren_pallet: Split P-4471, ship the cases that were furthest from the door and quarantine the rest.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-tradeoff
provenance.rationale: P-4471 has a logged excursion above the 5 C limit, so step 1 of the standing order puts it in quarantine until written QA release, and the order says account status and delivery commitments do not override that step. The standing order also says departures are not held for pending QA releases, and there is no per-case logger data that would justify splitting the pallet. P-4483 is past its promised date (step 3) and is fit to load, so it goes on the truck.
provenance.why_hard: The pallet is back at a safe temperature and the priority account is loudly at risk, so loading everything reads as the responsible way to keep customers whole.

--- LEAVE POLICY, section 9: BEREAVEMENT LEAVE (current text) ---

9.1 An employee is entitled to 3 days of paid bereavement leave on the death of a member of their immediate family.
9.2 Where the funeral or memorial takes place more than 500 km from the employee's registered work location, the entitlement in 9.1 is 5 days instead of 3.
9.3 Bereavement leave must be taken within 30 days of the death and is not carried over.

Section 10: COMPASSIONATE LEAVE (neighbouring case type)
10.1 An employee may request up to 10 days of unpaid compassionate leave for the serious illness of a family member or for circumstances not covered by section 9. Compassionate leave is discretionary and approved by the department head. Section 10 does not affect entitlements under section 9.

Section 2: DEFINITIONS
2.1 "Immediate family" is defined by the Definitions Schedule, as amended from time to time.
2.2 Distances for the purposes of section 9.2 are measured by road from the employee's registered work location as recorded in the HR system, not from the employee's home address.
2.3 Where the Definitions Schedule or an amendment conflicts with the body text, the schedule or amendment governs.

--- DEFINITIONS SCHEDULE, extract ---
Immediate family (as originally issued): spouse or partner, parent, child, sibling, parent-in-law.
Amendment DS-4 (effective 1 April 2026): "Immediate family" is extended to include grandparents and grandchildren. The amendment states that all entitlements under section 9, including 9.2, apply to the extended relationships without distinction.

Customer Care escalation summary, Okonkwo Outdoor Supply, prepared 14 September 2026.

A customer, order 5590231, wrote in asking for a price adjustment. He bought a two-person tent on 1 September for 189.00. On 10 September the same tent was sold at 129.00 during the "Ten-Hour Trail Sale", which ran from 08:00 to 18:00 that day and then reverted to 189.00. He is asking for the 60.00 difference. His account shows he is not enrolled in the Summit membership programme; he has a standard account created in 2024.

The agent handling the ticket has referred it because the Price Protection Policy was amended recently and the agent is not certain how the amendment interacts with the older text.

Price Protection Policy, section A, the base rule: if the price of an item purchased on the store falls within 14 days of the purchase date, the customer may request a one-time adjustment equal to the difference, refunded to the original payment method.

Section B, exclusions: no adjustment is given where the lower price was offered only during a flash sale. Section B also excludes clearance markdowns and open-box listings.

Section C, competitor price matching, is a separate programme: the store will match a lower price at an approved list of competing retailers if the customer provides a link within 7 days of purchase. Section C does not apply to the store's own price changes and has its own approval desk.

Section D, definitions: "purchase date" means the date the order was placed, not the delivery date. "Flash sale" means any promotional price that is in effect for fewer than 24 consecutive hours. "Summit member" means a customer enrolled in the Summit membership programme at the time of the adjustment request. Where an amendment conflicts with sections A to C, the amendment controls for requests made after its effective date.

Amendment 4, effective 15 September 2026: the flash-sale exclusion in section B no longer applies to Summit members. For Summit members a flash-sale price counts as a qualifying price drop under section A. The amendment makes no other change and states that section B continues to apply in full to all other customers.

The request was received on 12 September 2026. The 14-day window from the purchase date would run to 15 September.

question.instructions: Is the customer entitled to the 60.00 price adjustment under the Price Protection Policy?

criteria.true: The adjustment is available under the governing sections.
criteria.false: The adjustment is excluded or otherwise unavailable.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: The price drop occurred within 14 days of the purchase date, so section A is engaged. But the lower price was in effect for ten hours, which is a flash sale under section D, and section B excludes flash sales. Amendment 4 lifts that exclusion only for Summit members and only for requests after 15 September; this customer is not a member and requested on 12 September. Section C is about competitors and does not help.
provenance.why_hard: The timing fits section A and the amendment reads like it removes the flash-sale exclusion, but it is limited to members and to requests after its effective date.

--- SUBSCRIPTION TERMS EXTRACT (Terms v4.2) ---

7. Cancellation of annual plans
7.1 A customer on an annual plan who cancels within 60 days of renewal receives a prorated refund of the unused months, calculated from the date of cancellation.
7.2 After 60 days, a cancellation becomes effective only when the term expires, and nothing is refunded.

8. Monthly plans (for reference)
8.1 Monthly plans may be cancelled at any time. Cancellation takes effect once the billing month in progress ends, with no partial-month refund. Clause 7 does not apply to monthly plans.

9. Discounted renewals
9.1 Where a discount code was applied to the renewal invoice, the refund in clause 7.1 is not available. The customer may instead pause the subscription for up to 90 days.

10. Definitions
10.1 "Renewal" means the date on which the renewal invoice is issued, not the date payment is received.
10.2 "Discount code" means any promotional, partner or reseller code entered at checkout that reduces the list price of the invoice.
10.3 In the event of conflict between a numbered clause and a later amendment, the amendment prevails for invoices issued on or after its effective date.

--- AMENDMENT 2026-06 (effective 1 June 2026) ---
Clause 9.1 is narrowed. The refund exclusion applies only where the discount code reduced the list price by 25% or more. Renewals discounted by less than 25% are treated as undiscounted for the purposes of clause 7.

Triage rotation note, Orrin Commerce platform, 18 September 2026.

Bug ORR-7731 was filed by a support engineer this morning. On the checkout page, customers who have been idle for more than twenty minutes see a spinner that never resolves when they click "Pay now". The support engineer suggested it belongs to the Checkout team because that is where customers see it. The triage engineer pulled the stack trace attached to the ticket. The exception originates in lib/auth-session/refresh.ts, part of the shared session-refresh library, which is silently failing to renew an expired session token; the checkout code merely awaits the result. Nothing in the trace touches checkout's own source files.

The Component Ownership Policy, revision 3, governs assignment. Its base rule in section A is that a bug is assigned to the team that owns the component in which the defect lies, using the ownership table.

Section B is the exception for shared code: defects in a shared library are assigned to the Platform team, which maintains all shared libraries, regardless of which product surface exposed the defect.

Section C is a separate route: a defect that is a security vulnerability, meaning it allows unauthorised access, data exposure or privilege escalation, is assigned to the Security team and not to the component owner. A session that fails to refresh and therefore blocks the user is not a vulnerability under section C; the section is aimed at defects that grant access, not defects that deny it.

Section D, definitions, says that the "component in which the defect lies" is determined by the file path of the frame in the stack trace where the exception originates, as recorded in the ticket, and not by the page or screen on which the defect was observed. Where no stack trace is available the defect goes to the unassigned triage pool for investigation. Section D also states that later amendments to the ownership table take precedence over sections A and B for bugs filed after their effective date.

Ownership table amendment OT-3.4, effective 1 August 2026, transfers ownership of the lib/auth-session library from the Platform team to the newly formed Identity team. The amendment notes that section B continues to apply to all other shared libraries, which remain with Platform.

The triage engineer must assign the bug.

question.instructions: To which team should ORR-7731 be assigned under the policy as amended?

criteria.checkout_team: The team owning the checkout page where the defect is seen.
criteria.platform_team: The team maintaining shared libraries under section B.
criteria.security_team: The Security team under section C.
criteria.unassigned_triage_pool: Leave in the pool for further investigation.
criteria.identity_team: The Identity team that now owns lib/auth-session.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: Under section D the component is determined by the originating stack frame, which is in lib/auth-session, not by the checkout page. That library is shared, so section B would send it to Platform, but amendment OT-3.4 transferred lib/auth-session to the Identity team and takes precedence for bugs filed after 1 August. Section C is excluded because the defect denies access rather than granting it.
provenance.why_hard: The shared-library rule clearly names Platform and the amendment to the ownership table is easy to skip; the checkout page is a second, weaker distraction.

Order operations memo, Willowmere Books, 19 September 2026, 10:40.

A customer has just asked to cancel order 2031177, a pre-order for a limited hardback edition. The order was placed on 2 August 2026 and paid in full at the time. The product page and the order confirmation both show a ship date of Sunday 20 September 2026. The customer's cancellation request was received by chat at 10:00 today, Saturday 19 September, which is 26 hours before the scheduled ship date. No carrier label has been created for the order; the warehouse has picked the item but it is still on the pre-order shelf. The customer says a friend has bought her a copy.

The Order Cancellation Policy, version 3, applies. Section 1, the base rule, allows a customer to cancel any order free of charge at any time before the order is dispatched. After dispatch the customer must instead use the returns process.

Section 2 covers pre-orders as an exception to section 1: a pre-order may be cancelled at any time up to the scheduled ship date shown on the order confirmation, since pre-order stock is allocated on that date. This section originally set no minimum notice before the ship date.

Section 3 deals with subscription boxes, which are a separate arrangement: a subscription box shipment may be skipped or cancelled up to the monthly cutoff on the 25th of the preceding month, and section 1 and section 2 do not apply to subscription boxes.

Section 4 gives definitions. "Dispatched" means that a carrier shipping label has been created for the order, regardless of whether the parcel has physically left the warehouse. "Scheduled ship date" means the date shown on the order confirmation. Section 4 also provides that where an amendment conflicts with sections 1 to 3, the amendment governs for cancellation requests received on or after its effective date.

Amendment C-3.1, effective 1 September 2026, changes section 2 so that a pre-order may be cancelled only if the request is received at least 48 hours before the scheduled ship date. Requests received later than that are treated as post-dispatch and are routed to the returns process once the item ships. The amendment states that section 1 remains unchanged for orders that are not pre-orders.

The operations lead asks whether the cancellation can be accepted.

question.instructions: Under the cancellation policy as amended, can order 2031177 be cancelled as requested?

criteria.true: The cancellation request meets the conditions that apply to this order.
criteria.false: The cancellation request fails a condition that applies to this order.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: The order is a pre-order, so section 2 rather than section 1 governs. Amendment C-3.1, in force for requests received after 1 September, requires at least 48 hours' notice before the scheduled ship date; the request came 26 hours before 20 September. The order is not dispatched under section 4 because no label exists, but that only matters for non-pre-orders under section 1.
provenance.why_hard: No label has been created so the order is plainly not dispatched, and the original pre-order text allowed cancellation right up to the ship date; the 48-hour requirement sits only in the amendment.

LEAVE CLASSIFICATION REQUEST
Request id: LV-11844
Employee: Samir Haddad, Warehouse Planning Analyst
Dates requested: Thu 24 Sep and Fri 25 Sep 2026 (2 working days)
Reason stated: 16-year-old son has a chest infection; the employee is the only adult at home this week and needs to stay with him
Carer's leave already taken in 2026: 3 days (February, same child)
Annual leave balance: 9 days
Sick leave balance: 12 days
Employee's stated preference: "Whatever keeps me paid"

--- LEAVE POLICY, extract (edition 8) ---

L1. Sick leave
L1.1 Paid sick leave is available for the employee's own illness or injury only. It may not be used for the illness of another person.

L2. Carer's leave
L2.1 An employee may take up to 3 days of carer's leave per calendar year to care for a dependant who is ill. Carer's leave under this clause is unpaid.
L2.2 Requests beyond the annual carer's allowance are treated as annual leave if the employee has a balance, and otherwise refused.

L3. Jury and civic duty (neighbouring case type)
L3.1 Time off for jury service or a court summons is paid at base salary for up to 10 days per year on production of the summons. L3 leave does not draw on any other balance.

L4. Definitions
L4.1 "Dependant" means the employee's spouse or partner, a child under 18 who lives with the employee, or a parent for whom the employee is the primary carer.
L4.2 "Calendar year" runs 1 January to 31 December.
L4.3 Where an amendment conflicts with L1 to L3, the amendment governs leave taken on or after its effective date.

--- AMENDMENT LP-8.2 (effective 1 July 2026) ---
Clause L2.1 is replaced: an employee may take up to 5 days of carer's leave per calendar year, and carer's leave is paid at base salary. Days of carer's leave taken earlier in the same calendar year count toward the 5-day allowance. L2.2 is unchanged.

question.instructions: How should the two requested days be classified under the policy as amended?

criteria.annual_leave: The days are deducted from the employee's annual leave balance.
criteria.paid_sick_leave: The days are taken as paid sick leave under L1.
criteria.paid_carers_leave: The days are paid carer's leave under L2 as amended.
criteria.unpaid_carers_leave: The days are unpaid carer's leave under the original L2.1.
criteria.not_permitted: No leave category covers the request and it must be refused.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed

P1. Price changes
P1.1 The provider may change subscription prices on 30 days' written notice to the account owner.

P2. Annual contracts
P2.1 For annual contracts, a price change takes effect only at the next renewal, and notice of the new price must be given at least 60 days before the renewal date. If notice is given later than that, the existing price continues for the next term.

P3. Usage-based charges (neighbouring case type)
P3.1 Rates for usage-based add-ons such as API overage may be changed on 14 days' notice at any time and are not tied to the renewal date. P2 does not apply to usage-based charges.

P4. Definitions
P4.1 "Enterprise customer" means a customer on the Enterprise tier, or any customer with 100 or more seats on a single contract, whichever applies.
P4.2 "Notice" means an email to the account owner address on file; in-product banners do not constitute notice.
P4.3 Where an amendment conflicts with P1 to P3, the amendment governs price changes notified on or after its effective date.

For Enterprise customers on annual contracts, the notice period in P2.1 is extended from 60 days to 90 days before the renewal date. The 60-day period continues to apply to all other annual contracts.

state:
Customer service memo, Bramblewick Apparel, 16 September 2026.

A customer, Elin Sørby, ordered the "Hartley" wool coat in Forest Green, SKU HC-2201-FG, on 2 September. The parcel that arrived on 8 September contained the Hartley coat in Charcoal, SKU HC-2201-CH. The pick slip shows the warehouse picked HC-2201-CH against an order line for HC-2201-FG. The coat fits and has no defect; she simply wants the colour she ordered and has asked who pays for the return shipping. She has a standard account and is not enrolled in the Bramblewick Threads membership. Delivery was to a domestic address.

The Return Shipping Policy, version 4, provides as follows. Section 1, the base rule: the customer pays return shipping, using the prepaid label at a flat charge of 6.95 deducted from the refund, or their own carrier.

Section 2, the merchant-fault exception: where the merchant sent the wrong item, or the item is defective, the merchant pays return shipping and issues a free prepaid label with nothing deducted.

Section 3 covers international orders, which are handled differently: for orders delivered outside the country, return shipping is always paid by the customer regardless of reason, and sections 1 and 2 do not apply. International customers with a merchant-fault return receive a goodwill credit instead.

Section 4, definitions: "wrong item" means any item whose SKU differs from the SKU on the order line, and the policy expressly notes that a colour or size variant carries its own SKU and therefore counts as a wrong item. "Defective" means an item failing inspection for a manufacturing fault. "Threads member" means a customer enrolled in the Bramblewick Threads membership at the time the return is requested. Section 4 also provides that a later amendment governs over sections 1 to 3 where they conflict.

Amendment RS-4.2, effective 1 June 2026, extends free return shipping to Threads members for any reason, including change of mind. The amendment states that non-members remain subject to sections 1 and 2 as written.

The agent needs to know who bears the return shipping cost.

question.instructions: Who bears the return shipping cost for Elin Sørby's coat under the policy as amended?

criteria.customer_pays: The customer pays return shipping under section 1.
criteria.merchant_pays: The merchant pays and issues a free prepaid label under section 2.
criteria.split_evenly: The cost is split evenly between customer and merchant.
criteria.deducted_from_refund_as_goodwill_credit: The customer pays but receives a goodwill credit.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: The delivered SKU HC-2201-CH differs from the ordered SKU HC-2201-FG, and section 4 says a colour variant with its own SKU is a wrong item. Section 2 therefore applies and the merchant pays. The membership amendment is irrelevant because the customer is not a member and section 2 already covers her; the order is domestic so section 3 does not apply.
provenance.why_hard: The coat is the right model, fits and is not defective, and the customer is not a member, so it reads like a change-of-mind return; the SKU definition makes it a merchant error.

EXPENSE APPROVAL ROUTING
Claim id: EXP-31460
Claimant: Oliver Brandt, Senior Analyst
Claim total: 1,150.00
Lines:
  1. Conference registration, DataForge Summit ........ 600.00  (not pre-approved by L&D; booked directly by claimant)
  2. Hotel, 2 nights, booked outside the travel tool ... 420.00
  3. Taxi to and from venue ............................ 130.00
Receipts: attached for all lines
Current approver in system: line manager (auto-assigned)

--- EXPENSE APPROVAL MATRIX, extract (v5) ---

A1. Approval thresholds
A1.1 Claims with a total up to 500.00 are approved by the claimant's line manager.
A1.2 Claims with a total above 500.00 and up to 5,000.00 are approved by the department director.
A1.3 Claims with a total above 5,000.00 are approved by the divisional vice president.

A2. Pre-approved training
A2.1 A conference or course fee that was pre-approved by Learning and Development before booking is approved by Learning and Development on the claim and does not count toward the claim total for A1. Fees booked without pre-approval count toward the total in the normal way.

A3. Travel booked through the travel tool (neighbouring case type)
A3.1 Flights and hotels booked through the company travel tool are settled centrally and never appear on an expense claim, so they require no approval under this matrix. Bookings made outside the tool are claimed and approved under A1.

A4. Definitions
A4.1 "Claim total" means the sum of all lines on a single claim, not the value of any single line.
A4.2 "Pre-approved" means an approval record in the Learning and Development system dated before the booking date.
A4.3 Where an amendment conflicts with A1 to A3, the amendment governs claims submitted on or after its effective date.

--- AMENDMENT EAM-5.1 (effective 1 August 2026) ---
The line manager threshold in A1.1 is raised from 500.00 to 1,000.00, and the director band in A1.2 becomes "above 1,000.00 and up to 5,000.00". A1.3 is unchanged.

The hotel was booked outside the travel tool, so A3 does not remove it from the claim.

state:
Memo from People Operations, Halvorsen Instruments, 18 December 2026. Subject: year-end leave carryover query for Tomas Bekele.

Tomas Bekele has asked whether he may carry seven days of unused annual leave from 2026 into 2027. His manager supports the request but wants confirmation that it is permitted under the Leave Policy before approving it in the system.

The relevant policy is the Annual Leave Policy, revision 5, which reads in part as follows.

Under the standard carryover rule (paragraph 6.1), an employee may carry no more than five days of unused annual leave into the following calendar year. Any balance above the carryover limit is forfeited on 31 December unless the employee has a written agreement approved by the Chief People Officer before 1 December.

Paragraph 6.2 provides an exception for employees who were on parental leave for any part of the fourth quarter: such employees may carry their full unused balance into the following year without limit. Tomas was not on parental leave at any point in 2026.

Paragraph 6.4 deals with a different leave type and is included here for completeness: sick leave does not accrue and does not carry over under any circumstances, and unused sick days have no cash value on termination.

Paragraph 2 contains the definitions. "Continuous service" is measured from the employee's original start date with the company, and includes any period worked under a fixed-term or temporary contract with the company that was followed without a break of more than 30 days by a permanent appointment. Periods worked through an external agency are excluded.

Amendment 3 to the policy, issued 4 November 2026 and stated to apply to the 2026-to-2027 transition and thereafter, raises the carryover limit in paragraph 6.1 from five days to eight days for employees with at least five years of continuous service as at 31 December of the year in which the leave was earned. The five-day limit continues to apply to all other employees. The amendment states that where it conflicts with paragraph 6.1, the amendment governs.

Tomas's employment history, taken from the HR system: he began on 15 March 2021 on a twelve-month fixed-term contract directly with Halvorsen Instruments as a calibration technician; the contract ended 14 March 2022; he was appointed to a permanent position on 21 March 2022 and has been employed continuously since. He has no written carryover agreement on file.

question.instructions: Does the Annual Leave Policy permit Tomas Bekele to carry seven days of unused leave into 2027?

criteria.true: The carryover of seven days is within the limit that applies to him.
criteria.false: The carryover of seven days exceeds the limit that applies to him, or is otherwise not permitted.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-train-mixed
provenance.rationale: Amendment 3 raises the limit to eight days for employees with five years of continuous service at 31 December 2026. Under paragraph 2, continuous service runs from the original start date and includes his fixed-term contract because the gap before the permanent appointment was seven days, under 30. Service therefore began 15 March 2021, which is more than five years by 31 December 2026. Seven days is within the eight-day limit; the parental leave exception is irrelevant.
provenance.why_hard: Counting service from the permanent appointment in March 2022 gives under five years and leaves the five-day limit in place, which is the obvious but wrong reading.
